title: Regulatory register
description: The project-level machine output, and the half that travels into a consumer that never renders the markdown. Its field list was OWED by the design and is frozen here: the locks assert `mandate_id`, `dimension`, `merged_standard`, `verification_hint`, `source_requirement_ids`, `requires_counsel` and `conflict_ref` on every mandate row. Throughout this artifact `requirement` means a LEGAL OBLIGATION, never a product requirement.

legal_review_required.description: ALWAYS true, and const rather than boolean so it cannot be set to false. This survey reads instruments; it does not give legal advice, and a register that could declare itself not needing review would be doing exactly that.

instruments.description: Lens 1: one row per instrument, with the scope condition that made it apply and its binding force. An instrument applying IN PART says which part.

applies_part.description: Which part, where `applies` is `in-part`. An instrument applying in part and not saying which part has not been scoped.

applies_from_date.description: Lens 7 reads it: an instrument binding later is an architecture constraint now.

mandates.description: Lens 2, the MERGED block -- the one with no sibling precedent, which is why it is schematized here rather than inherited. A merge resolves to the strictest stated standard WITHIN one ordered dimension in one unit.

dimension.description: An ORDERED dimension only. `consent_basis` and `residency_constraint` are not comparable, so two requirements disagreeing there go to `conflicts` and never merge here.

merged_standard.description: The strictest stated standard in the group, in that dimension's own unit.

verification_hint.description: How a build phase would CHECK this mandate was met. A mandate nobody can verify is a sentence, not a constraint.

source_requirement_ids.description: EVERY obligation merged, cited. A merged standard resting on one citation is a merge that did not happen.

requires_counsel.description: True where ANY merged requirement carries it. Counsel does not stop being required because the merge tidied the group.

conflict_ref.description: Where this dimension also produced a conflict, the id of it. Null otherwise.

conflicts.description: Lens 3: pairwise within a dimension group where the constraints do not intersect, plus every non-comparable disagreement. ESCALATED, never resolved.

requirement_ids.description: At least two: a conflict is between obligations.

requires_counsel.description: A conflict between legal obligations is not a thing this survey resolves.

timing.description: Lens 4: every obligation carrying a duration, ordered by tightness, each with the trigger that starts its clock.

evidence.description: Lens 5: what must be logged, grouped by system surface, so the architecture learns it before the logging is designed.

absence.description: Lens 6, MANDATORY. Phrased as what was not FOUND across what was searched -- never that this product is unregulated.

jurisdictions_not_searched.description: Named, because a jurisdiction nobody searched is a different fact from one that returned nothing.

unretrievable_instruments.description: Named for the same reason: a paywalled instrument is a finding, not a gap.
